# Correcting the marked graph does not retain the required own-depth budget
of the new strict-face graph theorem, not to OC. Its arithmetic is
elementary and the obstruction holds for every choice of marked points.
Independent audit PASS:
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

Let n=1,d=2, let J=[-1/2,1/2], and take the actual convex body with
integer fibers at -1,0,1 equal to

    K_-1=K_1=[-1/2,1/2] times J,
    K_0=[-11/20,19/20] times J.

Explicitly use the convex hull of these three lifted rectangles. Its
projection is [-1,1]; the middle rectangle contains the Minkowski
midpoint of the endpoint rectangles, so these are exactly its integer
fibers. All fibers are full-dimensional. Their areas are 1,3/2,1,
their total M=7/2, and no fiber has area at least M/2=7/4.

Choose ANY marked points y_i=(t_i,s_i) in K_i whose full graph is
closed under the same-parity midpoint of the endpoint bases. Thus

    y_0=(y_-1+y_1)/2, in particular 2t_0=t_-1+t_1.     (1)

Let c_i be the raw ordinary halfspace depth of y_i in K_i. Two
coordinate halfspaces give the unconditional upper bounds

    c_-1<=1/2-|t_-1|,
    c_0 <=3/4-|t_0-1/5|,
    c_1 <=1/2-|t_1|.                                 (2)

These are actual rectangle cap areas because J has length one.
Allowing oblique caps can only lower c_i, so (2) remains an upper
bound for the full ordinary depth, with no orientation restriction.
Write e_-1=t_-1, e_0=t_0-1/5, e_1=t_1. Equation (1) gives

    2e_0-e_-1-e_1=-2/5.

The triangle inequality therefore yields

    |e_-1|+|e_0|+|e_1|>=1/5.

Sum (2) to obtain the uniform certified bound

    sum_i c_i <=7/4-1/5=31/20
               <14/9=Gamma_2 M,                    (3)

whose gap is exactly 1/180. Consequently it is impossible to choose
midpoint-affine marked points, or smaller certified raw depths at
those points, with total charge at least Gamma_2 M.

In particular, applying the marked-graph theorem with k=2 to any
such repaired graph supplies a numerical charge sum c_i/2 bounded
above by31/40, whereas OC asks for7/9. This does not say the marked
point's true mixed depth is that small; its other fiber contributions
can make it much larger. It says this proposed own-depth charge
certificate cannot reach the target, even after optimizing all its
marked points.

The same construction with J omitted gives a d=1 obstruction with
exact maximum total own depth31/20, below Gamma_1 M=7/4. In that
case interval raw depth is exactly the nearer endpoint distance,
and choosing all t_i=0 attains the bound. The d=2 argument needs only
the rigorous upper bound (3), not an unproved optimization formula
for oblique rectangle caps.

For any n>=1, take the Cartesian product in the integer coordinates
with [0,1]^(n-1). Each fixed binary copy contains the same parity-pair
constraint (1), so (3) applies separately to it. Summing gives

    total marked own-depth charge
       <=2^(n-1)31/20
       <Gamma_2 [2^(n-1)7/2].

There are k=2^n occupied parities. The claimed all-marked-point
obstruction therefore holds for every integer dimension, still with
no individual fiber of mass at least M/k=7/4. No affine change of the
lattice, limiting example, or numerical search is involved.

The source is separately OC-safe, as can be checked directly. In the
d=1 interval source the point (0,1/10) has raw depth33/20. To verify
the lower bound, let F(s)=min(1,max(0,1/2-s)) be an endpoint interval's
right tail. At t=1/10 and any integer tilt a, the two endpoint right
tails satisfy

    4/5<=F(t-a)+F(t+a)<=1.

For the lower bound use F(-s)=1-F(s) and its Lipschitz constant1;
for the upper bound use monotonicity and t>=0. The middle right
tail is17/20, so every right-oriented cap has mass at least33/20.
The endpoint left tails sum to at least1, and the middle left tail
is13/20, giving the same bound for every left-oriented cap. Vertical
caps through the point retain at least the middle and one endpoint,
of total mass5/2. The right-oriented cap with a=0 attains33/20.

Now take the product with the unit-length symmetric interval J.
At y=(0,1/10,0), condition any ambient cap on the half of J on which
its added-coordinate term is nonnegative. The remaining cap in the
interval source contains (0,1/10), and hence contributes at least
33/20. Integration over that half of J proves raw depth at least
33/40>7/9=Gamma_2 M/2. If the added-coordinate coefficient is zero,
the stronger full33/20 bound holds. For binary integer padding, use
the same point in any one copy and retain its contribution; the OC
target remains7/9 because both total mass and2^n gain the same factor.
No exact value for the two-dimensional mixed maximum is asserted.

Scope: this closes the route 'move all fiber centers to make every
midpoint identity exact while keeping total own-depth charge at least
Gamma_d M.' It does not close arguments that use additional paired
cap contributions or select a center outside the repaired marked graph.
